# sts (sts.origincloudapis.eu)

Guide: <https://docs.origincloud.eu/docs/iam/workload-identity-federation/index.html.md>

- **SecurityTokenService**: The security token service: it turns a token from an identity provider outside Origin Cloud, such as a CI job's OIDC token, into the access token of a `WORKLOAD` service account that trusts it through a federated credential.

## SecurityTokenService

The security token service: it turns a token from an identity provider outside Origin Cloud, such as a CI job's OIDC token, into the access token of a `WORKLOAD` service account that trusts it through a federated credential.

| Language | Client |
|---|---|
| Rust | `SecurityTokenClient::new(&client)` |
| Go | `stsv1beta1.NewSecurityTokenClient(client)` |
| TypeScript | `new SecurityTokenClient(client)` |

| RPC | Rust | Go | TypeScript | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AssumeServiceAccount` (`AssumeServiceAccountRequest`) | `assume_service_account` | `AssumeServiceAccount` | `assumeServiceAccount` | Assumes a `WORKLOAD` service account with an OIDC token. no MCP tool: Assuming a service account answers with its access token; a tool would put working credentials into the model's context, and an agent already has its own. CI jobs assume one through the SDKs and the CLI; requires `oidc_token` |

Field names: Rust uses the proto names (`size_gib`), Go protoc-gen-go's (`SizeGib`), TypeScript the JSON names (`sizeGib`).
